name: Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma
aliases: Punctate Keratoderma of the Palms and Soles

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Punctate Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple discrete punctate hyperkeratotic papules on the palms and soles
Histological confirmation showing epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other palmoplantar keratoderma subtypes by clinical and genetic evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic punctate hyperkeratotic lesions on palms and soles confirmed by histopathology, with exclusion of other keratoderma types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist in diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple discrete punctate hyperkeratotic papules on palms
pathognomonic.notes: Lesions typically range from 1 to 5 mm in diameter
searchTerms: small hard bumps on palms
multiple tiny thickened spots on hands

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple discrete punctate hyperkeratotic papules on soles
pathognomonic.notes: Lesions often coalesce under pressure areas
searchTerms: small hard bumps on soles
multiple tiny thickened spots on feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis
searchTerms: thickened outer skin layer with retained nuclei
skin biopsy showing thickened skin and abnormal cells

common.notes: May cause discomfort during manual activities or walking
searchTerms: mild cracks on palms and soles
slight fissuring on hands and feet

common.notes: Itching is usually mild to moderate
searchTerms: itching on thickened skin patches
localized itching on keratotic spots

common.symptomName: Callus formation on pressure points of palms and soles
searchTerms: calluses on pressure points of hands and feet
hardened skin spots on palms and soles
thick skin buildup at pressure sites

common.symptomName: Onset during adolescence or early adulthood

onset of skin issues during adolescence
early adult appearance of skin problems

discomfort related to fissures or infections

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea
genetic: Mutations in AAGAB gene (reported in some familial cases)
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic punctate keratotic papules on palms and soles

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse thickening of the entire palmoplantar skin rather than discrete punctate lesions
Linear or striate hyperkeratosis on palms and soles
Lesions follow lines of mechanical stress
Fungal infection with scaling and erythema

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Signs of secondary bacterial infection such as purulence or cellulitis
Severe pain impairing hand or foot function
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
